title: Reuse one policy-configured HTTP client for remote control calls
description:
## Finding

`ControlClient` stores only the address and creates a fresh reqwest client for every `HttpOrigin` request. Remote HTTPS calls therefore repeat DNS resolution, TCP/TLS setup, and connection allocation; the file's local-daemon one-connection-per-request rationale no longer applies.

## Evidence

* `crates/thegn-svc/src/control/client.rs:76` stores `ControlAddr` but no reusable transport client.
* `client.rs:1126` constructs `reqwest::Client::new()` for every request.

Repeated remote status/session/automation calls increase latency, CPU, FD/ephemeral-port churn, and lose one central place to enforce redirect, timeout, and body-limit policy.

## Required design

1. Build one cloneable policy-configured reqwest client per effective control configuration.
2. Reuse its connection pool across unary calls.
3. Centralize no-redirect, connect/request timeout, TLS, proxy, and response-limit policy.
4. Rebuild only when relevant endpoint/TLS/proxy configuration changes.

## Acceptance criteria

* Repeated same-origin requests reuse a connection in integration tests.
* Redirect and deadline/body-limit policies cannot differ by callsite.
* Config reload safely replaces the client without leaking old work.
* Local Unix/TCP behavior remains unchanged or uses an explicitly justified separate transport.

## Dependency mapping

Blocked by THE-273 (deadline/body-limit contract) and THE-280 (no-redirect security policy) — both landed.
